summary: Talquetamab-tgvs (Talvey) is a GPRC5D x CD3 bispecific T-cell engaging antibody for adults with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma after at least 4 prior lines including a proteasome inhibitor, an immunomodulatory agent, and an anti-CD38 antibody. It is given subcutaneously by actual body weight as 0.4 mg/kg weekly or 0.8 mg/kg every 2 weeks, each after step-up dosing (0.01 and 0.06 mg/kg, plus 0.4 mg/kg before the first biweekly dose), with pretreatment medicines and 48-hour hospitalization after each step-up dose. It carries a boxed warning for cytokine release syndrome and neurologic toxicity including ICANS and is available only through the Tecvayli-Talvey REMS. Distinctive on-target toxicities include dysgeusia, dry mouth, dysphagia with weight loss, and skin and nail disorders, alongside cytopenias, infections, hepatotoxicity, and embryo-fetal toxicity.
indications: Treatment of adults with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma who have received at least 4 prior lines of therapy, including a proteasome inhibitor, an immunomodulatory agent, and an anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody

dosage.d: Step-up dose 1: 0.01 mg/kg SC on Day 1; step-up dose 2: 0.06 mg/kg SC on Day 4; first treatment dose: 0.4 mg/kg SC on Day 7; then 0.4 mg/kg SC once weekly
dosage.t: Weekly until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity
dosage.n: Give pretreatment medicines before each step-up dose; hospitalize 48 hours after each step-up dose; keep at least 6 days between weekly doses

dosage.d: Step-up dose 1: 0.01 mg/kg SC Day 1; step-up dose 2: 0.06 mg/kg SC Day 4; step-up dose 3: 0.4 mg/kg SC Day 7; first treatment dose: 0.8 mg/kg SC Day 10; then 0.8 mg/kg SC every 2 weeks
dosage.t: Every 2 weeks until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity
dosage.n: Give pretreatment medicines before each step-up dose; hospitalize 48 hours after each step-up dose; keep at least 12 days between biweekly doses

dosage.d: Withhold for CRS, ICANS, serious infection, grade 3-4 cytopenias, or severe oral, skin, or other nonhematologic toxicity until recovery per labeling; permanently discontinue for recurrent grade 4 or life-threatening events
dosage.n: Step-up doses may be given 2 to 4 days after the prior dose (up to 7 days to allow resolution of adverse events)

admin: For subcutaneous injection only, based on actual body weight; give pretreatment medicines (corticosteroid, antihistamine, antipyretic) before each step-up dose
Hospitalize patients for 48 hours after each dose in the step-up schedule because of CRS and neurologic toxicity risk
Have tocilizumab and emergency support available; monitor for CRS, ICANS, and infection at each visit
Rotate injection sites; do not mix with other drugs in the same syringe
moa: Talquetamab-tgvs is a bispecific antibody that binds G protein-coupled receptor family C group 5 member D (GPRC5D) on myeloma cells and CD3 on T cells. By bridging T cells to GPRC5D-expressing myeloma cells, it triggers T-cell activation, cytokine release, and T-cell-mediated killing of myeloma cells. Because GPRC5D is also expressed on some healthy tissues including skin, nails, and oral mucosa (tongue, salivary glands), on-target off-tumor oral, skin, and nail toxicities occur.

absolute: Known serious hypersensitivity to talquetamab-tgvs or any excipient
relative: Pregnancy and breastfeeding (may cause fetal harm; avoid)
History of CNS disease or seizures (higher ICANS concern)
Severe cytopenias or hepatic impairment (limited data; monitor closely)
monitor: CRS signs (fever, hypotension, hypoxia) especially after step-up doses
Neurologic status for ICANS (confusion, dysphasia, tremor, depressed consciousness)
Oral intake, swallowing, taste changes, and weight
Skin, nails, and signs of infection; blood counts and liver tests

preg: Based on its mechanism of action, talquetamab may cause fetal harm through T-cell activation that can compromise pregnancy maintenance. There are no human pregnancy data and no animal reproductive studies. Verify pregnancy status before starting, advise effective contraception during treatment and for 3 months after the last dose, and avoid use in pregnancy.
lact: There are no data on talquetamab in human milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions including immune-mediated toxicity, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 3 months after the last dose.
renal: No labeled dose adjustment for renal impairment. Monitor closely in severe impairment and in patients with cytopenias or infection risk; no data in end-stage renal disease or dialysis.
hepatic: No labeled dose adjustment; monitor liver tests. Hepatotoxicity including transaminase elevation is reported; withhold or discontinue for severe hepatic events per labeling.

major: Live vaccines (avoid during treatment due to immunosuppression and infection risk)
Other myelosuppressive or neurotoxic therapies (additive cytopenia, infection, or neurotoxicity risk)
moderate: CYP substrates with narrow therapeutic index (cytokine release may transiently alter CYP activity during CRS; monitor)
minor: No major CYP-mediated interactions expected for a monoclonal antibody
interactions.food: No food effect (subcutaneous); maintain hydration and nutrition given dysgeusia, dry mouth, and dysphagia
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction; limit alcohol during CRS risk periods and with cytopenias or liver injury
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor CBC, liver tests, and infection markers; assess neurologic status with standardized ICANS grading; monitor weight and nutrition markers

serious: Cytokine release syndrome, including severe and life-threatening events (boxed warning)
Severe oral toxicities with weight loss and dehydration
emergency: Fever with low blood pressure, trouble breathing, or confusion after dosing (CRS/ICANS) - seek emergency care
Inability to swallow, severe mouth pain, or dehydration - seek urgent care
Fever with neutropenia or signs of sepsis - seek emergency care

monitoring: CRS and vital signs, with 48-hour hospitalization after each step-up dose
Neurologic status for ICANS using standardized grading at each visit
Oral cavity, swallowing, taste, appetite, and body weight
Skin and nails for rash, xerosis, exfoliation, and nail disorder
CBC, liver tests, and signs of infection; pregnancy status before starting
counsel: You will stay in the hospital for 48 hours after each step-up dose so the team can watch for fever, low blood pressure, trouble breathing, or confusion - report these at once
Taste changes, dry mouth, trouble swallowing, weight loss, skin rash or dryness, and nail changes are very common - report mouth sores, painful swallowing, or inability to eat or drink
Report fever, chills, cough, or any sign of infection promptly; avoid live vaccines and tell the team about all medicines
Do not drive or operate machinery if you feel confused, shaky, very tired, or have trouble speaking or thinking
Use effective contraception during treatment and for 3 months after the last dose; do not breastfeed during treatment and for 3 months after the last dose
pk: T-cell activation and cytokine elevation within days of step-up dosing; responses accrue over weeks
Peak concentrations after subcutaneous treatment doses with accumulation on repeat dosing
Elimination half-life on the order of days to weeks, consistent with an IgG-based bispecific antibody
Pharmacodynamic effects persist between weekly or biweekly doses; steady exposure with continued dosing
Refrigerate at 2-8 C (36-46 F) in original carton; do not freeze or shake; protect from light
pearls: First-in-class GPRC5D x CD3 bispecific; accelerated approval for myeloma after at least 4 prior lines including PI, IMiD, and anti-CD38 therapy
Boxed warning: CRS and neurologic toxicity including ICANS - available only through the Tecvayli-Talvey REMS with 48-hour hospitalization after step-up doses
Two maintenance options after step-up: 0.4 mg/kg weekly or 0.8 mg/kg every 2 weeks, both based on actual body weight
Hallmark on-target toxicities from GPRC5D on healthy tissue: dysgeusia, dry mouth, dysphagia with weight loss, plus skin disorders and nail changes - manage early to preserve nutrition
Embryo-fetal toxicity: verify pregnancy status, use contraception during and for 3 months after treatment, no breastfeeding
missed: Talquetamab is given on a supervised schedule. If a dose is delayed, give step-up doses 2 to 4 days after the prior dose (up to 7 days to allow adverse events to resolve) and maintain the minimum interval (6 days weekly, 12 days biweekly). Restart step-up dosing if the delay exceeds labeling limits; contact the treating team - do not double doses.
overdose: There is no specific antidote for talquetamab overdose. Expected effects are exaggerated CRS, neurotoxicity including ICANS, cytopenias, and infection. Provide intensive supportive care with CRS and ICANS management per labeling (including tocilizumab and corticosteroids), infection treatment, and prolonged monitoring. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
